steps.text: Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish with cooking spray. Set aside.

Melt butter in a large saucepan over low heat. Stir in vanilla. Add marshmallows; cook and stir until marshmallows are melted. Add cereal; stir to coat, then quickly transfer mixture to the prepared dish. Use a sheet of waxed paper to press mixture evenly into the dish.
Let set for 2 to 3 hours before cutting into 24 squares.

raw_recipe.headline: Marshmallow Crispie Bars
raw_recipe.description: These marshmallow cereal bars are made on the stovetop with 4 simple ingredients for sweet and chewy treats that are always a hit at birthday parties.
raw_recipe.name: Marshmallow Crispie Bars

review.reviewBody: VERY GOOD! I took the suggestion of adding an extra 1/2 cup of cereal, and the consistency was perfect...not too sticky and gooey. The vanilla really adds to the flavor, and using real butter is highly recommended. I do suggest either making a double batch for the 9X13 pan, or using a 9X9 or 8X8 for the original amount; I like thicker bars. Thanks Karen.

These were great! NOTE: don't let the butter burn, slow and steady wins this race! If the butter burns it will make these tough and of course bad tasting. I added half a cup of creamy PB to the marshmallow, and cocoa rice crispy instead of plain! Greased the pan and let sit over night. Then I double boil some chocolate chips and a TBSP of peanut butter and drizzled it over the done bars ... sooo yummy!! Great base of a recipe!!

How can you go wrong? For a fun twist, I used a pie tin, subbed some of the plain rice cereal with some fruity rice cereal, then topped with chocolate and butterscotch chips. I sliced like a pizza and the kids went wild for the new desert pizza. I've also used chocolate rice cereal and peanut butter chips. Go wild! The possibilities are endless! Try with different cereals, shapes and decorate for holidays.... Always quick and fun.

I added about six Hershey's kisses to the butter/marshmallow mixture for just a hint of chocolate. I also took others recommendations of adding an extra half cup of cereal and put the bars in an 8X8 pan instead of a larger pan. I tasted a little bit of the bars and they are very good.

I used a 10 ounce bag of marshmallows, 2 table spoons of vanilla and 6 cups of rice crispies. Turned out great. Also, give your spatula a quick coat of cooking spray when you’re ready to spread them into the pan. Makes it easier to make them good and flat, and evenly spread.
double the recipe and put in a 9x13 pan. Add 2 tsp of corn syrup and 1-2 Tbs of cocoa powder. Add melted chocolate to the top and it's perfectly gooey and yummy!
This was a really easy and great recipe! I added a dark chocolate drizzle (melted 75% dark chocolate bar) to balance out the sweetness and it was perfect!

Gooey = good. These are the kind they don't tell you about on the box of Rice Krispies. Great recipe! I also added the extra 1/2 cup of cereal per batch and doubled the batch. I made mine with my daughter today in the microwave, and added about a cup of crushed peppermint hard candies, and sprinkled red sugar on top and they were pretty and best of all, delicious.

I doubled the recipe & put in a 9X13 pan that I had coated with butter. I did my melting of the mallows in the microwave along with the butter & vanilla added. I just heated in 15 sec. intervals (high) for 1 min. 15 sec. (stirring after each 15 second heating) til it was easily smoothed when stirring; added the cereal & used a piece of parchment paper to pack it firmly into the buttered pan. So easy!

Add the extra 1/2 cup cereal like others suggested and use an 8x8 or 9x9 pan instead. I cant even imagine trying to use a 9x13 because they would be soooooo thin! For fun, we mixed in rainbow nonpareils (sprinkles) which made them even better!

This recipe was easy and turned out wonderful. I doubled the recipe and added a package of crumbled Oreos. Big rice crispie treats with Oreos. I just made sure everything was portioned out and ready before I started so I could get moving quickly. So yummy
I used OLD 4th of July frozen marshmallows (jumbo size cut into mini bits), and it was still delicious!! I used S'mores cereal, so I increased the marshmallows by 1/2 cup. Yum, yum, yum!
Very easy recipe to follow and delicious too! Before cutting, I melted different colored chocolates in icing bags and drizzled that across the top to make it more festive.
I loved the recipe. Great flavor with the vanilla extract. For younger kids. Try using cookie cutters to cut into different shapes. Makes it funny for them.
Love this recipe
pretty good
good and easy.
Easy peasy.
The only addition I made was I added mini marshmallows after the butter and marshmallows had incorporated with the Rice Krispies ... gives a nice surprise !

This recipe was fantastic, and I don’t even like Rice Krispie treats. I did add a 1/2 cup extra of cereal on the advice of other reviewers. The first time I made it, I only added 1/2 tsp of vanilla because I was a little nervous it would be too strong. The second time, I added the full teaspoon. Both were delicious with just the right texture and thickness. My 3 year old buttered the casserole dish and my 5 year old helped measure ingredients. Great recipe I will continue to make with my kiddos!
